title: Head-space P4 versus MODFLOW prepared-solve ownership reconciliation
question: Can the exact head-space factor-1/2 P4 safeguard qualified in G11/G17 be represented without semantic change inside the admitted F-GC38/F-GC39 continuous MODFLOW prepared-solve lifecycle?

prepared_solve_contract.nonconverged_iteration: do not rollback/discard X; update affine response and continue solve inside the same prepared solve

gates: Read the current branch versions of F-GC38 source and F-GC39 contract, not historical summaries only.
AST-audit the public Modflow6PreparedSolveSession method surface and confirm no admitted head-set/iterate-restore/rollback operation exists.
Confirm invalidate_without_finalize invalidates the session and does not restore X.
Confirm F-GC39 explicitly requires continuous X with no groundwater rollback between coupling iterations.
Reconstruct the exact first G11/G17 P4 contraction and prove the first accepted safeguard head is current + 0.25*(raw-current).

Classify whether that exact contracted head can become the MODFLOW coupling iterate using only admitted prepared-solve operations, without direct X mutation, session rollback, or whole-window reconstruction.
Direct mutation of the NumPy X pointer, even if technically possible, is outside the F-GC38/F-GC39 ownership contract and cannot count as an admitted implementation.
Do not reinterpret a response-space damping algorithm as P4 head-space equivalence without a separately preregistered qualification.
pass_interpretation: PASS means the contracts are compatible with exact G11/G17 P4 without adding a new state-control or reconstruction primitive.
falsification_interpretation: If exact P4 requires a state-control/reconstruction primitive absent from the admitted F-GC38/F-GC39 surface, classify the compatibility hypothesis as falsified. This does not falsify P4 or F-GC38 individually; it identifies a composition gap.
forbidden_mutation: F-GC38 or F-GC39 production/qualified contract semantics
